verifications.claim: A significant polar vortex split is expected in late March 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'A split in the Polar Vortex is becoming more likely toward the end of March.'; R1: 'late March Trends: Evolution of the Post-Collapse Weather Patterns'; R6: 'final collapse of the Polar Vortex as we head into March'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states split likely end of March; R1 and R6 describe ongoing split with late March impacts, aligning with expectation in late March 2026.

verifications.claim: The polar vortex split is likely to trigger a final, intense burst of cold air across the Upper Midwest and Northeast United States.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Upper Midwest into the Northeast could see one final blast of winter-like air'; R1: 'Polar Vortex core dropping into the United States... bringing along a wave of colder air'; R4: 'bursts of Arctic air to spill into the Midwest and Northeast'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly link split/disruption to final cold burst specifically in Upper Midwest/Northeast.

verifications.claim: The disruption of the high-altitude, cold-trapping vortex will break the circulation into smaller, mobile cores.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Polar Vortex is clearly split into two distinct cores... breaking the Polar Vortex into two separate cores'; R2: 'splits into two smaller vortexes... smaller lobes of the vortex periodically splitting off'; R6: 'full Polar Vortex split, dividing the high-altitude circulation into two distinct cores'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe high-altitude vortex disruption/split creating smaller, separate cores.

verifications.claim: The polar vortex split potentially causes temperatures 20-30°F below normal in some areas.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'temperatures 20 to 30 degrees F lower than normal for this time of year'
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly matches the exact temperature deviation range linked to Polar Vortex core/split event.
